messages.content: i like the book i am reading, but when someone asks why, i do not know what to say.
you do not have to know every reason to enjoy it. is there a small part you want to read about when you open it?
i like being in the room with the people in the story. they do not do much, but i want to know what they say next.
that gives you a way to explain it. you enjoy being with the people in the story, even when there is not much happening.
can a story be good if nothing large happens?
yes. some stories make us want to keep reading because of the people, their words, or the way a place feels. something large does not have to happen for a person to enjoy a story.
write my answer using only what i said about the book.
i like being with the people in the story. they do not do much, but i want to hear what they say next.
would that sound like i know them in real life?
in a conversation about a book, people will usually understand that you mean the people in the story. if you want to make it clear, keep in the story in your answer.
now make it one sentence.
i like being with the people in the story and finding out what they say next.
thanks. i do not need to explain the whole book.
that sentence gives your reason without telling the whole story.
there is a chair between the table and the window. where is it?
it is in the space between the table and the window.
does that tell us the color of the chair?
no. the sentence gives the place of the chair, not its color.
now i move the table to another room. is the chair still between the table and the window?
not in the same way. the table is no longer in that room. if the chair has not moved, it is still near the window, but the old sentence no longer gives a clear picture of the room.
can you say the chair moved because the sentence changed?
no. the table can move while the chair does not. then we may need a different sentence to say where the chair is.
use words i know for that explanation.
the chair can stay where it is while the things around it move. then we may need different words to say where it is.
now the chair is under the table in the other room.
then you have given a new place for the chair too. it is now under the table in the other room.
why not keep saying it is near the window?
you gave new information that changes its place. the answer should use the new information, rather than keep the first place.
only give where the chair is now.
it is under the table in the other room.
write a story about someone returning a book even though she has not finished it. use a simple reason.

a girl had a book from her friend and had read only the first few pages. her friend asked for it back because he wanted to read it with his sister. the girl wanted to keep reading, but she knew the book was his. she put a small piece of paper at her place so she could remember the page, then wrote the page number in her own book. she took the piece of paper out before giving the book back. she told her friend that she had enjoyed the start and would like to read more another time. he said they could talk about that after he and his sister had finished.
why did she write down the page number?
so she could remember where to begin if she read the book again later.
did her friend say she could keep the book now?
no. he asked for it back and said they could talk about another time later.
make her request clear without saying the book is hers.
i enjoyed the start of your book. may i read more of it another time, after you and your sister are done?
can she be sad to return it and still do what she said she would?
yes. she can feel sad that she has to stop reading and still return the book. her feeling does not change whose book it is.
finish with her choosing something else to read at home.
after returning the book, she looked at her own shelf. she chose a short story she had not read in a while and sat near the window.
my new neighbor sent a message saying welcome to the street. i want a short reply.
thank you for the kind welcome. i am happy to be here.
i do not want to say how i feel yet. i have only just moved.
thank you for the kind welcome. it is nice to hear from you.
can i ask their name without saying i forgot it? i have not met them.
yes. you can say: thank you for the welcome. may i ask your name?
that sounds a little hard for a simple message. can i give my name first?
yes. giving your name first can make the question feel like a simple start to the conversation.
my name is not needed in the example. give me only the first words so i can put my name after them.
you can write your name after this short start: hello, my name is
then what should i write after my name?
you can add a full stop, then write: thank you for the welcome. what is your name?
now only give the last two sentences.
thank you for the welcome. what is your name?
i took four books from my shelf and put them on my desk. then i returned one to the shelf. how many of those books are on the desk?
three of those books are on the desk.
then i took two different books from the shelf and put them on the desk too.
now there are five books from your shelf on the desk: the three that stayed, and the two you added.
how many different books did i take from the shelf during all that?
six different books: the first four, then two different books later.
why is that not the same as the number on the desk?
one of the six went back to the shelf. a book can have been taken from the shelf without still being on the desk now.
what if i take that same returned book out again?
then six of those books are on the desk. the number of different books you have taken is still six, because this time you took a book already in that group.
how many books did i put back on the shelf from the information i gave?
one book went back to the shelf. later, you took that same book out again.
can you know how many books are still on my shelf?
no. you have not given the number that was on the shelf at the start.
only tell me how many of those books are on the desk now.
six books.
what is the difference between i like tea and i would like tea?
i like tea says that you enjoy tea. i would like tea usually says that you want tea, often as a request now.
if someone asks what i want to drink, which is a clear answer?
i would like tea is a clear answer to that question.
can i like tea but not want it now?
yes. you could say: i like tea, but i would like water now.
why is that not wrong?
what you like in general can be different from what you want now. you can enjoy tea and choose another drink today.
give me that explanation in one short sentence.
you can enjoy tea and still choose a different drink now.
now make it about reading and drawing.
i like reading, but i would like to draw now.
does that mean i do not like books now?
no. your choice to draw now does not mean your feeling about reading has changed.
only give a kind request for water.
i would like some water, please.
write a story about a note that was useful before a room changed.

a father left a note for his son saying that the key was under the cup on the table. before the son came home, the father cleaned the room and put the cup on a shelf. he also moved the key to a small container near the door, but forgot the note. when the son read it, he looked under the cup and found nothing. he asked his father whether the key had been moved. the father remembered the note, showed him the new place, and wrote a new message for the next morning.
was the son wrong to read the note?
no. it was information his father had left for him. the problem was that the place had changed and the note had not been changed with it.
why should the new note give the key place rather than the cup place?
the son needs the key. knowing where the cup is does not tell him where the key is after they have been moved apart.
write the new note.
the key is in the small container near the door.
should the father say that is where it will always be?
only if he knows he will keep it there. the story gives the place now, not a rule for every day.
finish with him making a useful choice about later changes.
he put the new note where his son would see it. if he moved the key again, he would change the note too.
what is the short reason for changing the note?
the note should give the place where the key is, rather than the place where it used to be.
my friend moved to another town. we still talk, but i miss seeing them at the end of the day.
you can still be close through conversation and miss being in the same place at the end of the day.
i miss telling them something before i even think of it as a story.
the small things could reach them right when they happened. now you may have to hold them until you talk.
yes. i do not want a list of things to try. i just wanted to say that.
i hear you. it is the easy conversation at the end of the day that you miss.
can you help me say that in a message to my friend?
i miss telling you the small things right when they happen. we still talk, but i miss seeing you at the end of the day.
can you make it about being in the same place, rather than the end of the day?
i miss telling you the small things right when they happen. we still talk, but i miss being in the same place.
can that sound like i want them to move back?
it can be read as telling them how you feel, rather than asking them to move back. if you want, you can add that you are not asking them to change their plan.
give me that last idea in two short sentences.
i am not asking you to change your plan. i just wanted you to know what i miss.
